text:
**LiFePO4 (LFP) is the better choice for most people.** NMC only makes sense in a few cases, covered below.

**Where LiFePO4 wins**
- **Cycle life:** LFP stations are typically rated for 3,000-6,000 cycles to 70-80% capacity. NMC units are rated for roughly 500-1,000, and one source says up to 2,000. Daily cycling would wear out a 500-cycle NMC battery in about 1.4 years, versus about 8 years for a 3,000-cycle LFP one ([UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/), [PowerStations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Failure behavior:** In lab tests, LFP cells failed more mildly. They peaked at about 259°C versus 731°C for NMC, and released smoke without flames. It's not fireproof. One study found LFP reached thermal runaway sooner in an overcharge test ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/), [UnpluggedWatts](https://www.unpluggedwatts.com/lifepo4-vs-nmc-power-station/)).
- **Price:** The premium has mostly disappeared. One retailer database shows a median of $0.55/Wh for LFP versus $0.95/Wh for NMC, and per cycle LFP is much cheaper ([PowerStations.reviews](https://powerstations.reviews/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc)).
- **Availability:** Most current models are LFP. In one database, 48 of 54 models are LFP, and most NMC units are legacy products ([OutageMath](https://www.outagemath.com/guides/lifepo4-vs-nmc/)).

**Where NMC wins**
- **Weight:** NMC cells hold more energy per kilogram. In finished stations the gap shrinks to roughly 10-16% per pound, because the case, inverter and fans weigh the same either way. Some LFP stations are even lighter per watt-hour than some NMC ones.
- **Occasional use:** If you only cycle a unit a few dozen times a year, NMC's cycle rating won't run out first. A lightweight compact or a heavily discounted NMC unit can be fine in that case.

**Things the chemistry doesn't decide**
- **Cold weather:** Most stations of both types refuse to charge below 32°F. Check the manual for the specific model.
- **Cycle ratings:** Check the end point. "3,000 cycles to 70%" promises less than "3,000 to 80%".
- **Fit:** Pick for capacity and output first, then chemistry.
